subject: Urgent: Hosted API p95/p99 spike after deploy — hotkey eviction suspected
messages:
From: Alex Barnes <alex@velvetretail.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: API latency / p95 and p99 regressions — urgent

Naomi / Redwood team,

We started seeing a large regression in p95/p99 latency for our live traffic right after your 07:55 UTC deployment this morning. Metrics: our p95 for generate-token increased from ~180ms to ~680ms and p99 jumped to ~2.4s. Error rate also ticked up ~0.7% (mostly upstream timeouts). This maps to a customer-facing page load regression across several high-traffic routes.

We run high-volume, low-latency inference and we believe this is related to your KV/prefix cache behavior — we saw a surge in full-model cold starts and a period of very high token fanout for keys we call "hot_session_identity_*". The pattern looks like hotkey eviction / cache coherence problem where many requests simultaneous miss and cause a burst of work on GPUs.

Attached is a perf dump and a couple of flamegraphs. Please advise immediate mitigation (we're open to short-term rollbacks, temporary quota increases, or any routing workarounds). Our side is prepared to throttle non-critical traffic, but we need an ETA to restore p95/p99 to baseline.

Alex
Engineering Lead, Velvet Retail
--

—Naomi

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: API latency / p95 and p99 regressions — urgent

Quick findings from the first 40 minutes of triage:

- We observed a sharp drop in prefix-cache hit rate at 07:56:12 UTC across the hosted-api fleet serving Velvet Retail. The cache TTL config for prefix groups was changed in the 07:55 deploy (rolling config): default TTL reduced from 15m -> 2m to lower memory pressure.
- Several heavy prefixes (hot_session_identity_*) were not pinned; eviction triggered simultaneous cache-fill requests. This caused a continuous-burst cold-KV path: massive KV fetches + KV-to-GPU kernel warm-up at scale which raised p95/p99 tokens.
- We also saw elevated serialization queueing on a subset of inference nodes while the KV miss storms were ongoing.

Immediate actions taken:
1) Rolled back the TTL change in config for the affected prefix group (propagated within 5 minutes) — hit rate recovered slowly but we saw immediate reduction in error rate.
2) Temporarily added a pin for the top 12 hot prefixes for Velvet Retail (manual pin config).
3) Throttled cache fill concurrency for the cluster to reduce thundering-herd risk (soft limit).

Next steps:
- Full mitigation: we should rework the prefix eviction policy to include autoscaling-aware pinning for identified hotkeys and add a hotkey warmup path to avoid GPU cold starts on miss fanout.
- Post-incident: run a pre-deploy check that compares hotkey landings vs TTL changes.

Logs attached: minimal perf traces and the cache metrics. Dylan
SRE — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: API latency / p95 and p99 regressions — update and next steps

Alex — thank you for the quick signal and for the dump. Wanted to share the current state and recommended customer-facing ops steps:

- Status: TTL rollback + manual pinning reduced p95 from ~680ms to ~200ms over ~18 minutes; p99 improved from ~2.4s to ~420ms and error rate dropped close to baseline.
- Recommended temporary steps for Velvet Retail (optional): 1) Throttle lower-priority inference routes for the next 3 hours; 2) Enable request sampling on high-fanout prefixes and provide logs; 3) If acceptable, schedule a short maintenance window tomorrow for us to run a controlled warmup job to repopulate KV entries for your top prefixes.

We will follow up with a draft post-mortem and a permanent mitigation plan (policy change + pre-deploy warning). If you'd like, we can provide a short customer-facing timeline for your leadership.

Thanks — Marissa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Team — brief exec summary for finance/support:

- Incident: p95/p99 regressions for Velvet Retail caused by an unintended TTL reduction in a config rollout that led to hotkey eviction and a KV miss storm.
- Impact: short-term customer-facing degradation (p99 peaked ~2.4s). Resolved to baseline after rollback + pinning; partial mitigation applied within ~12 minutes, full stabilization ~30 minutes.
- Root cause: unsafe TTL tweak in prefix config without a hotkey impact check.
- Action items (owners):
  * SRE (Dylan) — build autoscaling-aware pinning + limit cache fill concurrency (2 weeks).
  * Product (Karthik) — pre-deploy static analysis and a hotkey-change gated check (1 sprint).
  * CS (Marissa) — post-incident customer notes and a proposal for a goodwill credit (immediate).

Marissa, please propose a goodwill credit (suggestion: 10% credit for August invoice) and I will sign off if customer impact validates. Naomi, keep Alex posted and offer the warmup window tomorrow as proposed.

Jonas
VP, Operations — Redwood Inference
